transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I hope I'm not wasting your time, it's probably nothing too serious. But what brings me in is, well, I just keep messing up little things. Nothing major! Just... silly slip-ups, I guess. Like, um, I'll write the wrong time down on a sign-up sheet for a class at the senior center. Or I'll be out in the garage, and I'll measure a board once, but I'll still cut it a hair short just because I sort of skipped over the small print on the tape measure. 

It's a little embarrassing to even bring up, honestly, making careless mistakes at my age. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Have you noticed these types of slip-ups your entire life, or is this a relatively new change for you?

Well, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it's not exactly a new thing. I mean, it's not like I suddenly changed or anything. 

Actually, even way back in elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was a bright kid, you know? But... well, they'd also mention that I'd forget my books or lose my homework sometimes. And, um, they said I had a habit of staring out the window unless someone reminded me to pay attention. 

But kids are like that, right? Daydreaming a bit? It wasn't anything malicious, I just... needed a little extra help staying on track, I suppose. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
When you are in situations where you are expected to sit still for a while, like at a meeting or watching a movie, do you find it difficult to remain seated or do you feel a need to fidget?

Oh, well... I really try to be respectful when other people are talking, so I wouldn't say I'm disruptive or anything like that. I'd hate to be a bother to anyone. 

But... I suppose if I'm sitting through a whole meeting, or even just having a quiet evening at the condo, I do sometimes get this... well, sort of an ants-in-my-pants feeling? I just get the urge to get up, maybe check on something in the other room, or just putter around a little bit. 

It's nothing extreme, just... needing to stretch my legs or keep my hands busy for a second, you know? I always try to do it quietly so I don't disturb anyone. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I explained that okay.

latest_inference.note: The patient's lifelong history of inattentive symptoms (forgetting homework, daydreaming) combined with current reports of careless mistakes and physical restlessness (fidgeting, needing to move) is highly suggestive of Adult ADHD. The symptoms do not appear to be secondary to mood or anxiety disorders, as the patient describes these as lifelong traits rather than episodic changes.
